historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun describes a Zamis or Zemis as a type of religious leader or priest in his book 'The Muqaddimah'. He mentions that these individuals were responsible for the care and maintenance of shrines and tombs of saints, and were considered to have a special status and influence in the community.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun was a renowned Arab historian, philosopher and sociologist. His magnum opus, 'The Muqaddimah', is considered a seminal work in the field of historiography and sociology.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi, in his book 'Ittfāq al-hūdā fī ʾl-tarīkh al-kāmil bi-shamāʾil Ḥijāz al-kabīr', describes the Zamis as hereditary leaders of certain Sufi orders in Hejaz. He notes that they were responsible for the spiritual guidance of their followers, and their authority was recognized by the local population and senior religious figures.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi was a prominent Egyptian historian, geographer and scholar. His major work, 'Ittfāq al-hūdā', is a comprehensive history of Egypt and the Islamic world.
